title: Old-Time Parsnip Storage
subtitle: 1917 USDA Wisdom
desc: Old-time parsnip and salsify storage inspired by USDA Farmers' Bulletin 879, Home Storage of Vegetables (1917), rewritten for today: frost turns parsnips sweeter, so leave part of the row in the garden under a thick straw or leaf mulch and dig as needed, and keep dug roots trimmed in a cold, humid root cellar near 32–40°F so they don't shrivel.

title: How to Pressure Can Chicken
subtitle: USDA Tested Method
desc: How to safely pressure can chicken following the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: raw pack or hot pack the pieces with 1¼-inch headspace, then process boneless pints 75 minutes and quarts 90 minutes, or bone-in pints 65 and quarts 75, at 10 lb weighted gauge or 11 lb dial gauge (0–1,000 ft), adjusting for altitude. Ready-to-eat meat for the winter pantry.

title: How to Dry Hot Peppers
subtitle: Easy Winter Pantry Spice
items: String thin ones to air dry
desc: How to dry hot peppers at home: pick ripe, unblemished cayenne or chili peppers, wear gloves, string thin-walled peppers to air dry in a warm, airy spot or dry halved peppers in a dehydrator at 125–135°F until brittle, then store whole or ground in airtight jars away from light. Simple food preservation for homemade chili flakes.

title: Winter Care for Chickens
subtitle: Keep Your Flock Healthy
desc: Winter care for backyard chickens: keep fresh water unfrozen, block drafts while leaving roof vents open to stop moisture, use deep dry litter, give a little extra feed on cold days, gather eggs often so they don't freeze, and watch combs for frostbite. Practical homestead skills for a healthy, self-sufficient flock.

title: Test Your Garden Soil in Fall
subtitle: Plan a Better Spring
items: Send to a soil test lab
Add lime in fall if needed
desc: How to test your vegetable garden soil in fall: take small samples 6 inches deep from 10 or more spots, mix them in a clean bucket, air dry and send to your local soil testing lab. Fall results give lime and compost time to work before spring planting. An easy beginner garden tip for bigger harvests.
